question: Why do rural Nigerian midwives often need to manage animal bites and stings?

options.A: They are frequently the primary healthcare providers available in rural communities.
options.B: Government policy requires midwives to handle all veterinary emergencies.
options.C: Snakes and insects only attack pregnant women in rural areas.
options.D: Traditional healers refuse to treat any form of animal injury.

explanation: Because primary health centers are often understaffed, midwives frequently provide the first emergency care for bite and sting patients. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T7#BMP110_U7_T7_h1)

question: How does the growing uterus affect the diaphragm in late pregnancy?

options.A: It pulls the diaphragm downward toward the pelvic floor.
options.B: It pushes the diaphragm upward into the chest cavity.
options.C: It paralyzes the muscle fibers of the diaphragm completely.
options.D: It wraps around the diaphragm to restrict all chest movement.

explanation: As the baby grows, the uterus pushes upward, changing the shape and space inside the chest. [learn more](BMP121_U1_T1#BMP121_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the correct order of steps during a single manual peritoneal dialysis exchange?

options.A: Infuse fresh fluid, allow it to dwell, then drain the old fluid.
options.B: Infuse fresh fluid, drain immediately, then allow the dwell phase.
options.C: Allow the fluid to dwell, drain the old fluid, then infuse fresh fluid.
options.D: Drain the old fluid, infuse fresh fluid, then allow it to dwell.

explanation: An exchange must first remove the old, saturated fluid through draining before infusing fresh solution for the dwell period. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T9#BMP216_U1_T9_h5)

question: About how many cotyledons are usually visible on the maternal side of a full-term placenta?

options.B: 5 to 10

explanation: The maternal surface of the placenta is divided into roughly 15 to 20 distinct lobes called cotyledons. [learn more](BMP210_U5_T1#BMP210_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the combined action of the lumbrical and interosseous muscles in the hand?

options.A: Flexing the knuckles while straightening the finger tips
options.B: Spreading all five fingers outward in a flat fan
options.C: Pronating and supinating the entire wrist joint
options.D: Pulling the whole hand backward toward the forearm

explanation: These small muscles bend the knuckles at the base while keeping the rest of the fingers straight, creating a natural hand posture. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T10#BMP111_U3_T10_h6)

question: Why must an intravenous injection of ergometrine be given very slowly rather than as a rapid push?

options.A: To prevent a sudden and dangerous spike in blood pressure
options.B: To stop the uterus from contracting too softly
options.C: To give the drug time to dissolve completely in the syringe
options.D: To ensure the baby does not absorb the drug through breast milk

explanation: Fast intravenous injection of ergot alkaloids causes acute and severe hypertension and can trigger stroke. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T2#BMP213_U1_T2_h4)

question: When should a midwife expect to use empiric antimicrobial therapy?

options.A: Only after all laboratory test results are fully confirmed
options.B: At the very end of a failed course of narrow-spectrum treatment
options.C: When the patient shows an allergy to standard first-line drugs
options.D: Before laboratory culture and sensitivity results are ready

explanation: Empiric treatment starts right away based on clinical signs and common local germs while waiting for lab tests to confirm the exact cause. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T1#BMP124_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is the partograph designed to show all labor parameters on a single sheet?

options.A: To save printing costs for the hospital administration and the government
options.B: To provide a quick visual trend that highlights any developing complications
options.C: To eliminate the need for writing any narrative notes in the case file
options.D: To ensure patients can easily fill out their own medical records

explanation: Grouping all observations together lets the midwife spot warning signs immediately by looking at how the lines trend over time. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why must a midwife check leg movement before allowing a post-Caesarean mother to walk to the bathroom?

options.A: To confirm the regional block has worn off enough to prevent falls
options.B: To check if her stitches are healing without any wound infection
options.C: To make sure she has not developed a blood clot in her calf
options.D: To test if her kidneys are producing enough waste products

explanation: Remaining numbness and muscle weakness increase the risk of the mother collapsing if she tries to stand up too early. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T8#BMP213_U2_T8_h6)

question: What percentage of total blood volume does plasma typically make up?

options.A: 30 percent
options.B: 70 percent
options.C: 45 percent
options.D: 55 percent

explanation: Plasma accounts for roughly 55 percent of total blood volume, while cellular elements make up the remaining 45 percent. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T1#BMP111_U5_T1_h1)

question: A 30-year-old woman comes to the clinic with irregular spotting for two months and mild cramps. What is the first action the midwife should take?

options.A: Schedule an immediate surgical procedure
options.B: Administer high-dose hormone tablets to stop the flow
options.C: Perform a pregnancy test to rule out gestational causes
options.D: Prescribe strong oral iron supplements and send her home

explanation: A pregnancy test is always a priority for women of reproductive age experiencing irregular bleeding to check for conditions like ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T4#BMP310_U3_T4_h3)

question: A mother asks if she should give plain water to her two-month-old baby on a hot afternoon. How should you respond?

options.A: Advise adding a small pinch of sugar and salt to the water
options.B: Suggest giving boiled water only during the hottest afternoon hours
options.C: Recommend fresh fruit juice as a safer alternative to plain water
options.D: Explain that breast milk contains enough water even in hot weather

explanation: Breast milk has a high water content that fully satisfies a baby's thirst, and extra water can introduce germs. [learn more](BMP227_U1_T4#BMP227_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which simulation tool is best described as a healthy actor portraying a pregnant woman?

options.A: Standardized patient
options.B: High-fidelity manikin
options.C: Low-fidelity task trainer
options.D: Computerized fetal monitor

explanation: Standardized patients are trained actors who simulate real patient behaviors, helping students practice communication and history-taking skills. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T8#BMP312_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why can TORCH infections be tricky to spot in pregnant women just by looking at them?

options.A: Physical signs only appear after delivery occurs
options.B: Maternal blood pressure hides any signs of infection
options.C: Mothers often show no symptoms or only mild, flu-like signs
options.D: Symptoms are completely hidden by normal pregnancy discomforts

explanation: Many pregnant women experience either no symptoms at all or very mild illness, which is why routine lab screening during antenatal care is so important. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T9#BMP221_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which way of giving nifedipine is discouraged because it can cause a sudden, dangerous drop in blood pressure?

options.A: Standard oral swallowing
options.B: Slow intravenous drip
options.C: Sublingual puncturing
options.D: Intramuscular injection

explanation: Puncturing capsules to absorb them under the tongue causes the drug to enter the body too fast, leading to dangerous low blood pressure. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T4#BMP213_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which piece of equipment significantly increases water loss through the skin of a preterm infant?

options.A: Pulse oximeter probe
options.B: Nasal cannula tubing
options.C: Radiant warmer
options.D: Mechanical ventilator

explanation: Radiant warmers use heat lamps that cause water to evaporate quickly through the delicate skin of sick newborns, increasing their fluid needs. [learn more](BMP220_U3_T5#BMP220_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why might a midwife check a client's hemoglobin level before recommending a copper intrauterine device?

options.A: Blood tests are legally required before touching any reproductive organ
options.B: Copper IUDs can increase menstrual bleeding, which may worsen existing anemia
options.C: Anemia causes the copper to dissolve too quickly inside the uterine cavity
options.D: Low hemoglobin levels prevent the IUD from staying in the correct uterine position

explanation: Copper-bearing devices often cause heavier periods, making baseline anemia checks important for safe management. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T2#BMP224_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why must pregnant women eat protein every day instead of relying on stored reserves?

options.A: Hormones destroy stored protein during the first trimester
options.B: Stored protein is instantly converted into body fat
options.C: The body cannot store extra protein for later use
options.D: The placenta blocks the release of stored proteins

explanation: The body has no major storage depot for proteins, so regular dietary intake is needed to meet daily needs. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T2#BMP118_U2_T2_h1)

question: A thirteen-year-old first-time mother comes to the clinic with continuous urine leakage after a difficult home delivery. What condition does this history suggest?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Ectopic pregnancy
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Obstetric fistula

explanation: Continuous leakage of urine following prolonged obstructed labor in a young mother is the classic presentation of an obstetric fistula. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T6#BMP310_U1_T6_h3)

question: Besides physical wound care, what is an important way midwives can support parents of a baby with spina bifida?

options.A: Providing emotional counseling and linking them with community support
options.B: Instructing them to avoid all future pregnancies permanently
options.C: Guiding them on how to finance private hospital expansion
options.D: Encouraging them to isolate the child from community events

explanation: Families need emotional support, reassurance, and practical advice to help them handle the long-term care of a child with a congenital condition. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T4#BMP220_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the correct way to fix a writing mistake in a paper clinical record?

options.A: Tear out the entire page and start the nursing notes fresh
options.B: Draw a single line through the error, correct it, then sign and date
options.C: Scrape the ink off the paper using a razor blade until it disappears
options.D: Apply thick liquid correction fluid over the error and write on top

explanation: A single line keeps the original entry legible underneath, ensuring transparency, while liquid paper hides information which looks suspicious in court. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h6)

question: A newborn revived with naloxone forty minutes ago starts breathing slowly again. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The delivery room temperature is too low
options.B: The umbilical cord was clamped too early
options.C: The initial dose of naloxone has worn off
options.D: The baby is experiencing normal newborn sleep

explanation: Naloxone has a short action time, so the longer-acting opioid can start slowing the breathing down again after the antidote wears off. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it not enough to just treat the symptoms of shock in an emergency?

options.A: Patients will develop an allergy to the IV cannula
options.B: Resuscitation fluids cannot work without extra drugs
options.C: Blood pressure will rise too high if the root cause is ignored
options.D: The underlying cause will keep making the patient worse

explanation: If the source of bleeding, infection, or vascular spasm is not stopped, the patient will continue to lose ground despite fluid therapy. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h5)

question: What causes the strong fishy smell often noticed in bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Acids made by dying protective bacteria
options.B: Secondary fungal fermentation inside the vagina
options.C: Breakdown of excess blood from minor bleeding
options.D: Chemical compounds (amines) produced by overgrowing bad bacteria

explanation: The breakdown of proteins by anaerobic bacteria creates volatile amines, which cause the distinct fishy odor. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T9#BMP310_U2_T9_h2)

question: A pregnant patient with persistent asthma expresses fear that using her prescribed steroid inhaler will cause birth defects. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Advise her to stop all medications immediately and rely solely on breathing exercises until after delivery
options.B: Explain that poorly controlled asthma causes low oxygen that is much more dangerous to the baby than the inhaler
options.C: Suggest replacing the prescription inhaler with herbal teas to completely avoid chemical exposures
options.D: Tell her to double her dose only when she feels short of breath to make up for missed days

explanation: Maintaining good oxygen levels through proper medication use protects the fetus far better than avoiding safe maintenance therapies. [learn more](BMP221_U4_T11#BMP221_U4_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of occupational health?

options.A: Treating only acute workplace injuries in factories
options.B: The physical, mental, and social well-being of workers
options.C: Managing hospital budgets for employee insurance
options.D: Increasing daily industrial production quotas

explanation: Occupational health looks at the whole person across all areas of well-being, not just physical safety or factory injuries. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T1#BMP126_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is feeding through a nasogastric tube preferred over long-term drip feeding when possible?

options.A: It absorbs much faster through the liver and kidneys.
options.B: It removes the need to check blood levels.
options.C: It completely removes any risk of lung infection.
options.D: It keeps the gut working and protects the stomach lining.

explanation: Using the digestive tract keeps the gut wall healthy and stops bacteria from escaping into the bloodstream. [learn more](BMP120_U5_T1#BMP120_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is the medical term for an open sore in the upper part of the small intestine?

options.A: Pyloric stenosis
options.B: Gastric ulcer
options.C: Duodenal ulcer
options.D: Esophageal tear

explanation: A duodenal ulcer forms in the duodenum, which is the first segment of the small intestine right after the stomach. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T5#BMP125_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is the time right after childbirth a crucial period for watching mothers with heart conditions?

options.A: Large fluid shifts occur as blood returns from the uterus to general circulation
options.B: Breastfeeding stops the heart from beating at a normal regular rhythm
options.C: The mother is usually too tired to notice if she is having chest pain
options.D: Blood pressure drops instantly to zero after the baby is delivered

explanation: After delivery, extra blood flows back into the general circulation from the contracted uterus, which suddenly increases the workload on the heart. [learn more](BMP125_U2_T1#BMP125_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why are physical signs of anxiety often missed during routine antenatal visits?

options.A: Pregnant women never experience physical pain from stress
options.B: Blood tests always reveal the exact anxiety score instantly
options.C: Midwives are legally barred from asking about physical complaints
options.D: They look very similar to normal physical discomforts of pregnancy

explanation: Physical signs like fatigue, poor sleep, and aches are common in pregnancy, making it easy to overlook them as signs of mental distress. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T4#BMP223_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the standard recommended midwife-to-patient ratio for a woman in active labor?

options.A: One midwife to one woman
options.B: One midwife to six women
options.C: Two midwives to one woman
options.D: One midwife to ten babies

explanation: A woman in active labor requires continuous support, monitoring, and emotional encouragement, making a one-to-one ratio the global gold standard. [learn more](BMP312_U2_T1#BMP312_U2_T1_h3)

question: What does local ownership mean for a community health facility?

options.A: The community views the facility as their own and takes responsibility for it
options.B: Foreign donor agencies hand over financial audits to village chiefs
options.C: The local government transfers the land title directly to the attending midwife
options.D: Private businessmen take over the daily management of pharmacy supplies

explanation: Local ownership means the community takes pride in and responsibility for the health facility and its services. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T4#BMP117_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does data completeness mean when filling out maternity registers?

options.A: Every nurse has signed the attendance register daily
options.B: The computer system has finished backing up files
options.C: All patients in the community have visited the clinic
options.D: All required fields in the register are properly filled

explanation: Completeness requires that no mandatory information is left blank when documenting patient care. [learn more](BMP123_U5_T1#BMP123_U5_T1_h2)

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in SMART campaign objectives?

options.A: Managed
options.B: Mandatory
options.C: Medical
options.D: Measurable

explanation: Measurable objectives allow you to clearly track your progress and know if your campaign targets were met. [learn more](BMP227_U2_T1#BMP227_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the recommended time to wait before trying to get pregnant again after completing treatment for choriocarcinoma?

options.A: Only three months
options.B: Exactly five years
options.C: No waiting period is needed
options.D: At least one year

explanation: Delaying pregnancy for twelve months allows healthcare providers to monitor hCG levels accurately without confusion from a new gestation. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T9#BMP221_U1_T9_h5)

question: A woman at 32 weeks is having contractions, but her temperature is high and her membranes have been ruptured for three days with foul discharge. Why is salbutamol contraindicated?

options.A: Infection makes the mother's heart immune to the drug's effects
options.B: Stopping an infected uterus from emptying puts the mother at severe risk
options.C: Fever completely destroys the chemical makeup of salbutamol
options.D: Salbutamol stops antibiotics from working inside the mother's bloodstream

explanation: When chorioamnionitis is present, the priority is delivering the baby to clear the infection, not holding the pregnancy inside. [learn more](BMP213_U1_T6#BMP213_U1_T6_h7)

question: How do the ischial spines usually feel during a vaginal examination in an android pelvis?

options.A: Completely flat and impossible to feel
options.B: Blunt and widely separated
options.C: Prominent and sharply pointing inward
options.D: Soft and movable under gentle pressure

explanation: Prominent, sharp, and inward-pointing ischial spines reduce the space of the midpelvis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T4#BMP210_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the maximum recommended number of cup detachments or pull failures before stopping a vacuum procedure?

options.A: Three
options.B: Five
options.C: One
options.D: Ten

explanation: Exceeding three pop-offs or failed pulls indicates that the vacuum method is not working and risks fetal injury if continued. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h5)

question: When should a midwife apply standard precautions during clinical duties?

options.A: Whenever hospital management is conducting an inspection
options.B: Only when caring for patients diagnosed with HIV or hepatitis
options.C: During every patient interaction regardless of diagnosis
options.D: Exclusively when assisting with complicated surgical deliveries

explanation: Standard precautions are universal, meaning they protect you and the patient during every single clinical encounter, no matter the recorded diagnosis. [learn more](BMP116_U5_T4#BMP116_U5_T4_h2)

question: Why is it important for the lecturer to narrate the 'why' alongside the 'what' during a procedure?

options.A: It prevents students from falling asleep.
options.B: It replaces the need to read textbooks after class.
options.C: It helps students connect clinical actions to underlying anatomical and safety principles.
options.D: It proves the lecturer knows difficult medical terms.

explanation: Explaining the reasoning behind an action builds critical thinking, ensuring students understand clinical safety rather than just copying movements blindly. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T5#BMP312_U3_T5_h3)

question: What type of organism causes gonorrhea?

options.A: A Gram-negative diplococcus
options.B: A double-stranded DNA virus
options.C: A Gram-positive spirochete
options.D: A flagellated protozoan parasite

explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a Gram-negative diplococcus bacterium that infects mucosal membranes. [learn more](BMP310_U2_T4#BMP310_U2_T4_h1)

question: A postpartum mother recovering from an emergency Caesarean section complains of sudden left calf pain, swelling, and tenderness on her second day post-op. What should the midwife suspect?

options.A: Uterine subinvolution
options.B: Normal postpartum muscle cramp
options.C: Deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Superficial wound dehiscence

explanation: Calf pain, swelling, and tenderness on one side are classic signs of deep vein thrombosis, which needs an urgent medical review. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main risk of failing to properly record vaccine and IPTp doses in clinic registers?

options.A: It automatically changes the gestational age of the unborn baby
options.B: It can lead to missed doses or unnecessary repeat administrations
options.C: It stops the laboratory from running routine blood hemoglobin tests
options.D: It causes the expiration date of the remaining drug stock to shorten

explanation: Without clear records, subsequent healthcare providers cannot tell which protective doses the woman has already received. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized complication of severe zinc deficiency in pregnancy?

options.A: Permanent maternal vision loss
options.B: Intrauterine growth restriction
options.C: Prolonged or difficult labor
options.D: Premature rupture of membranes

explanation: While severe zinc deficiency causes growth restriction, prolonged labor, and membrane complications, permanent blindness is primarily associated with vitamin A deficiency, not zinc. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T11#BMP118_U2_T11_h6)

question: How is the structure of the hepatic portal system different from normal blood vessels?

options.A: It bypasses the heart completely to speed up circulation
options.B: It places a capillary bed between two venous blood vessels
options.C: It pumps deoxygenated blood directly into body tissues
options.D: It connects two large arteries without any capillaries

explanation: Unlike standard circulation where veins return blood straight to the heart, a portal system features capillaries situated between veins. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T19#BMP111_U5_T19_h1)

question: What is the primary cause of varicose veins?

options.A: Lack of red blood cells in the vessels
options.B: Incompetent or damaged venous valves
options.C: High pressure inside the capillary beds
options.D: Thickening of the outer arterial wall

explanation: When valves fail to seal properly, blood flows backward and pools, causing veins to bulge and twist into varicose veins. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T16#BMP111_U5_T16_h5)

question: Which two main hormones are deficient in primary adrenal insufficiency?

options.A: Estrogen and progesterone
options.B: Cortisol and aldosterone
options.C: Thyroxine and calcitonin
options.D: Insulin and glucagon

explanation: Addison's disease specifically involves the destruction of the adrenal cortex, leading to a shortage of glucocorticoids like cortisol and mineralocorticoids like aldosterone. [learn more](BMP216_U2_T7#BMP216_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is the main feature of a missed abortion?

options.A: Severe heavy bleeding starts suddenly before any pain begins
options.B: Active uterine contractions push out the pregnancy immediately
options.C: The pregnancy tissue stops growing inside the uterus but is not expelled
options.D: The placenta delivers normally while the fetus remains alive

explanation: In a missed abortion, the fetus has stopped developing or died, but the cervix stays closed, so the tissue stays inside the uterus instead of coming out right away. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T6#BMP221_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why are NSAIDs often very effective for managing postpartum uterine afterpains?

options.A: They lower local prostaglandin levels which drive uterine cramping
options.B: They stop breast milk production to reduce pressure on the abdomen
options.C: They force the placenta to deliver faster after the baby is born
options.D: They put the mother to sleep so she cannot feel any contractions

explanation: Uterine cramps are triggered by local prostaglandins, so drugs that block these chemicals provide great relief. [learn more](BMP124_U3_T2#BMP124_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the traditional cardinal signs of acute inflammation?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Calor
options.C: Rubor
options.D: Dolor

explanation: Cyanosis refers to a bluish discoloration from lack of oxygen, which is not part of the standard signs of inflammation. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T5#BMP111_U6_T5_h5)

question: What is another common name for parasympathomimetic drugs?

options.A: Adrenergic drugs
options.B: Cholinergic drugs
options.C: Anticholinergic drugs
options.D: Sympathomimetic drugs

explanation: Parasympathomimetic drugs mimic the parasympathetic nervous system and are widely known as cholinergic drugs because they work with acetylcholine. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T4#BMP124_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why does prolonged obstructed labor frequently lead to obstetric fistula in teenagers?

options.A: Surgeons accidentally cut the urinary tract during emergency deliveries
options.B: Pressure from the baby's head cuts off blood supply to surrounding tissues, causing necrosis
options.C: Hormonal imbalances prevent the bladder from contracting properly
options.D: The sudden rush of amniotic fluid dissolves the walls of the uterus

explanation: When the baby gets stuck for too long, the soft tissues between the birth canal and bladder are crushed against the pelvic bone, leading to tissue death and fistulas. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T2#BMP320_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of problem solving in nursing and midwifery practice?

options.A: To bridge the gap between actual situations and desired outcomes
options.B: To minimize the need for documentation during shifts
options.C: To strictly follow hospital administrative rules at all times
options.D: To ensure doctors make all final clinical decisions

explanation: Problem solving is fundamentally about identifying where a patient is versus where they need to be, and taking steps to close that distance safely. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T9#BMP110_U3_T9_h1)

question: How long should a midwife monitor a patient after giving naloxone?

options.A: Until the placenta is delivered
options.B: Only for ten minutes
options.C: Until the end of the week
options.D: At least two hours

explanation: Because naloxone wears off quickly, monitoring the patient for at least two hours helps catch any return of breathing problems. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T4#BMP213_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which hormone primarily maintains the uterine lining and prevents menstruation during early pregnancy?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Progesterone keeps the endometrium thick and prevents it from shedding, which stops menstrual bleeding. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which part of the neuron receives incoming signals from other cells?

options.A: Dendrites
options.B: Nodes of Ranvier
options.C: Myelin sheath
options.D: Axons

explanation: Dendrites are the branched extensions of a neuron that act like antennae to pick up chemical and electrical messages from neighboring cells. [learn more](BMP121_U5_T5#BMP121_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is NOT a recommended strategy for midwives working to reduce mental health stigma?

options.A: Educating community members about the medical basis of mental illness
options.B: Treating psychological issues as personal weaknesses or spiritual flaws
options.C: Providing compassionate, non-judgmental care during checkups
options.D: Normalizing conversations about emotional wellbeing in antenatal classes

explanation: Labeling mental health conditions as personal weaknesses builds stigma and stops women from seeking help. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T7#BMP223_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why is giving timely feedback so important after a staff member completes a delegated task?

options.A: It is required to update the hospital financial payroll
options.B: It reinforces good clinical practices and corrects mistakes early
options.C: It prevents staff from ever asking questions again
options.D: It allows the manager to publicly punish poor workers

explanation: Constructive feedback helps staff grow professionally by validating correct actions and addressing errors before they affect patient safety. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is it important for a midwife to recommend locally available and affordable foods during antenatal counseling?

options.A: To discourage the consumption of foreign supplements
options.B: To reduce the workload of the antenatal clinic staff
options.C: To make sure the mother gains as much weight as possible
options.D: To ensure the dietary advice is realistic and practical for the family's budget

explanation: Recommendations must fit within the financial reality of the household for the mother to maintain them. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T16#BMP212_U1_T16_h6)

question: A teenager has had severe heavy periods ever since her very first cycle. Along with a blood count, which test is most important?

options.A: Endometrial biopsy
options.B: Hysterosalpingography
options.C: Coagulation screen
options.D: Cervical cytology smear

explanation: When heavy bleeding starts right from menarche, it often points to an underlying clotting disorder like von Willebrand disease, making a coagulation screen essential. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T3#BMP310_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the recommended initial action when a breastfeeding mother is prescribed a new medication?

options.A: Advise the mother to permanently wean her baby immediately
options.B: Switch the baby to full formula feeding without checking guidelines
options.C: Tell her to discard all expressed milk for the next two weeks
options.D: Consult a verified reference guide on drug safety during lactation

question: What is the main role of the skin in regulating body temperature?

options.C: It produces all the heat needed to keep internal organs warm.
options.D: It controls the nervous system signals that dictate metabolism.

question: What primary tool did Taylor use during time studies to measure work?

options.D: A thermometer

question: What is a core safeguarding duty for a midwife during routine clinical work?

options.D: Identifying physical or behavioral red flags during routine assessments

question: What does the term "brain drain" refer to in the context of Nigerian tertiary health care?

question: A midwife assesses a laboring woman and notices contractions lasting 60 seconds every 2 minutes with no resting time between them. What is the main concern here?

question: What is a typical starting dose for oral methyldopa therapy in pregnancy?

options.A: 250 milligrams
options.B: 1000 milligrams
options.C: 5 milligrams
options.D: 50 milligrams

explanation: Starting at 250 milligrams two to three times daily helps the patient tolerate the medication and minimizes side effects like drowsiness. [learn more](BMP213_U3_T1#BMP213_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why might a healthy term newborn show a temporarily weak suck right after birth?

options.A: Permanent damage to the hypoglossal nerve
options.B: Exposure to labor medications or birth fatigue
options.C: Congenital absence of the hard palate
options.D: Severe dehydration from pregnancy

question: How does a Nigerian midwife apply the Alma-Ata principle of community participation in her work?

options.A: Ordering medical equipment directly from overseas manufacturers without consultation
options.B: Involving local women and leaders in planning health education and outreach programs
options.C: Requiring all pregnant women to relocate to city hospitals before delivery

question: Which type of dietary iron is absorbed most efficiently by the human digestive tract?

options.A: Inorganic iron found in mineral water
options.B: Heme iron from animal products
options.C: Non-heme iron from green vegetables
options.D: Chelated iron powders in processed foods

question: A client comes for a routine follow-up visit at 28 weeks. Which set of assessments must the midwife record on her card?

options.A: Detailed surgical history from her childhood years
options.B: Only her current home address and next of kin details
options.C: Weight, blood pressure, urinalysis, and fundal height
options.D: Only her church denomination and occupation history

question: What should be done if the forceps blades do not lock together easily after placement?

options.C: Wait two hours for the baby to rotate spontaneously

question: Which ethical principle is the main reason we keep research participant information confidential?

options.A: Institutional efficiency
options.B: Financial compensation
options.C: Scientific advancement
options.D: Respect for persons

explanation: Respect for persons means honoring human autonomy and a person's right to privacy. This is the foundation of research confidentiality. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T9#BMP225_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a positive sign of pregnancy?

options.A: Visualization of the gestational sac on ultrasound

options.D: A positive home urine test for hCG

question: Which national system collects the community health records that midwives gather in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Community Database

question: At what point in pregnancy can the syphilis bacterium cross the placenta to infect the fetus?

question: What is the main reason standard Gram staining fails to work on Mycobacterium tuberculosis?

options.B: The bacteria only stain when exposed to direct sunlight

question: What immediate clinical action should be taken when a laboring woman's cervical dilatation line crosses over the action line?

question: Why is a hierarchical folder structure better than keeping all files in one large folder?

explanation: Breaking documents down into categorized folders and subfolders makes navigation intuitive and prevents administrative chaos. [learn more](BMP123_U2_T3#BMP123_U2_T3_h5)

question: What do we call the study of how the body handles a drug after it is given?

options.A: Pharmacodynamics
options.B: Pharmacokinetics
options.C: Pharmacoepidemiology
options.D: Pharmacogenomics

explanation: Pharmacokinetics is the study of how a drug moves through the body, covering absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T6#BMP124_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why are corticosteroids given to a pregnant woman at thirty-one weeks who is at risk of early preterm delivery?

options.A: To prevent heavy bleeding after the baby is born
options.B: To lower the mother's elevated blood pressure levels safely
options.C: To stop uterine contractions and prolong the pregnancy to term

question: During which stage of pregnancy do clinicians exercise the highest caution when prescribing medications like metronidazole?

options.A: Third trimester

options.C: First trimester
options.D: Postpartum period

question: Why is the planning phase so important in clinical midwifery practice?

options.A: It eliminates all potential risks in labor wards
options.B: It connects identified health problems to purposeful actions
options.C: It allows midwives to prescribe medications independently
options.D: It replaces the need to document daily vital signs

explanation: Planning takes the diagnosis from the assessment stage and turns it into an organized strategy for clinical care. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T4#BMP120_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is judgment from healthcare workers dangerous for pregnant women using substances?

options.A: It forces the baby to metabolize drugs at a much faster rate

options.C: Judgmental words instantly cure physical drug dependence

question: Which chemical structure is found in both cephalosporins and penicillins?

options.A: A peptide backbone
options.B: A thiazolidine ring
options.C: A beta-lactam ring
options.D: A hydrocarbon chain

explanation: Both cephalosporins and penicillins belong to the beta-lactam antibiotic family. They share this central ring structure, which allows them to fight bacterial infections. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T3#BMP124_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are regular community meetings important for building lasting partnerships across different sectors?

options.A: They ensure that health workers make all decisions alone

question: During an antenatal health talk, what practical footwear advice should a midwife give pregnant farmers?

options.B: Walk barefoot to feel the soil texture and avoid slipping.
options.C: Wear open sandals to keep the feet cool during hot farm work.

question: What is a key difference between menopausal mood changes and clinical depression?

options.A: Menopausal mood changes always last for exactly ten continuous years.

options.C: Menopausal mood changes never include any feelings of sadness.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication that needs careful monitoring after a baby undergoes resuscitation?

question: What does a sudden weight gain over one or two days usually indicate for a patient with cirrhosis?

question: Which international body sets the essential competencies required for basic midwifery education and practice?

question: Why does air get trapped inside the air sacs in someone with emphysema?

question: What is NOT a recommended instruction for a client recovering from a sterilization procedure?

question: Which diagnostic method is most commonly used for a quick check of malaria antigens in a busy antenatal clinic?

question: How do routine clinic audits help improve midwifery documentation standards?

question: Why is accurate data collection important after conducting an outreach clinic?

question: Why must Nigerian midwives understand local cultural beliefs when discussing family planning?

question: Which part of the respiratory system is mainly affected by fluid and inflammation in pneumonia?

question: What is the main action a Village Health Worker should take when encountering a complicated medical case?

question: Which laboratory markers are most commonly monitored to assess inflammation and treatment response in osteomyelitis?

question: When insulin is severely lacking, which metabolic process directly leads to a buildup of ketone bodies in the blood?

question: What is the standard approach when stool tests are not available at a rural antenatal clinic?

question: What is the main goal of a cardiac rehabilitation program after hospital discharge?

question: What is a frequent long-term physical consequence of sexual violence reported by women in clinics?
